key_insight: A hybrid front nanocone + embedded nanohole architecture boosts light trapping in thin-film silicon by reducing reflection and increasing internal optical confinement.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical route to higher-efficiency, thermally robust thin-film silicon solar cells without changing the absorber material itself.
method: FDTD optimization of nanocone and nanohole geometry
Coupled electrical device modeling under optimized doping
evidence_signal: At the optimized point, the device achieved 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% FF, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retained up to 45 °C.
watch_item: The structure depends on precise nanoscale fabrication and alignment, so manufacturability and process variability may limit real-device translation.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
